newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba says German economic recovery uneven so far.
newsitem.headline: Buba says German economic recovery uneven so far.

text.p: Germany's fledgling economic recovery has delivered uneven rewards with most of the benefits going to companies in west Germany, the Bundesbank said on Tuesday.

In its monthly report for December, the German central bank said that although the economy has remained on a growth course since the middle of the year, east Germany has not been able to continue boosting output and restructuring in the region has started to slow.
"The normalisation of the growth process, a dying down of the building boom and increasing economic stability, presents new problems to the east German economy," the report said.
The Bundesbank also said that companies engaged in export markets are benefitting more than those whose business is closely linked to the domestic economy.

The report said domestic demand remains restrained and that it remains to be seen how quickly the recovery will take root in regions and sectors that have so far lagged behind the rest of the economy.

The Bundesbank also cautioned that a stronger dollar has not been the entire key to stronger economic growth. It said that labour costs have improved due to increases in productivity at the same time that wages climbed only moderately.
The Bundesbank said the key to continued economic growth is an increase in investment. But investment has so far failed to benefit from climbing corporate profits.
